implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: a field segment is malformed unless it contains exactly one '=' character
unresolved_intent.rationale: values cannot contain '=' per spec, so a second '=' in a segment cannot be a legal value; rejecting on count!=1 rather than splitting on the first '=' catches this case before it silently produces a value containing '='

unresolved_intent.decision: encode validates each message strictly: type must be dict-present and match [A-Z]+, fields must be a list of exactly-2-element [key,value] lists, key must match [a-z]+, value must be a string free of '|' and '='
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec says a message that 'could not be produced by a legal frame' must error too, so encode needs its own full shape/charset validation independent of decode's parser

unresolved_intent.decision: an empty frame string is always ERROR; an empty field segment (e.g. from consecutive '|' or a trailing '|') is ERROR because it contains zero '=' characters
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec explicitly lists an empty string as a malformed frame, and a segment with no '=' cannot be a valid key=value field

unresolved_intent.decision: any top-level JSON that is not an object, has a direction other than exactly 'decode'/'encode', or has frames/messages not typed as a list, is ERROR before any per-item processing begins
unresolved_intent.rationale: keeps the atomicity guarantee uniform: structural failures fail the whole batch the same way a single bad frame does, per AC-PA-06

unresolved_intent.decision: a message object is accepted as long as it has 'type' and 'fields' keys with valid values; extra unexpected keys are not rejected
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec only defines the message shape as {type, fields} but does not state that additional keys must cause an error, so the stricter reading (reject extras) was not chosen to avoid inventing an unstated constraint

compilation_report.constraint_handling: r2: second blind run of the same model on the same canonical package (ADR-027 intra-model variance)
